Class CommAPI (AAComm; AAComm C#): An API for handling communication with the AACommServer executable. The API provides low-level send/receive capabilities + special functionality. All *synchronous* functions are mutually-locking, and should not be called from multiple threads Proper work-flow: (see usage details at every function description) 0. subscribe to events: Long operations: OnLongOperationStarted / OnLongOperationEnded, General Error: OnCommsError, Push: OnPushMessageReceived (TBD) 1. StartAACommServer 2. TestConnection (not mandatory, can be used to determine ControllerType) 3. Connect 4. Send and/or SendReceive (both safe from any thread, in any combination — independent FIFO pipelines for ordinary messages) 5. Disconnect 6. CloseAACommServer (not mandatory)
Signature: class AAComm.CommAPI

Members:
- ctor .ctor()
  Default CTOR. The client negotiates the wire protocol with AACommServer at connect time: binary first, transparently falling back to the legacy ASCII protocol if the server is an old ASCII-only build. Read Protocol after Connect to see what was negotiated.
- property System.Version AACommServerVersion { get; }
  AACommServer version, as reported by AACommServer upon Connect Valid only when IsConnected is true (0.0.0 if disconnected)
- method AAComm.Services.CommSessionHandle CaptureSession()
  Captures the current connection, or returns null when disconnected.
- method System.Void CloseAACommServer(System.Boolean = False)
  Synchronous function NOT thread-safe (protected vs. re-entry) called at the end of API usage. Sends "ShutDown" command to AACommServer. (AACommServer process will terminate, if current client is the last one) Disconnects if connected
- method AAComm.Shared.ConnectResult Connect(AAComm.Services.ConnectionData, System.Boolean = False)
  Synchronous function, tries to establish a required connection NOT thread-safe (protected vs. re-entry) Call state: NOT connected Exit state: Connected if success, Clean disconnected state if failure initializes containers: ControllerIdentityContainer and ControllerMessagesContainer
- method AAComm.Shared.ConnectResult ConnectSilent(AAComm.Services.ConnectionData)
  Synchronous function, tries to establish a required connection NOT thread-safe (protected vs. re-entry) Call state: NOT connected Exit state: Connected if success, Clean disconnected state if failure should be used for connecting in order to download FW in boot mode does NOT query the controller for any data (except clear RS-232 buffer, if RS-232 channel)
- property AAComm.Services.ConnectionData CurrentConnectionData { get; }
  API state: get current ConnectionData (NULL if not connected)
- method System.Void Disconnect()
  Synchronous function NOT thread-safe (protected vs. re-entry) clears queue and sends Disconnect request to AACommServer all messages left in send queue will NOT be processed clears containers: ControllerIdentityContainer and ControllerMessagesContainer
- method System.Void Dispose()
  Releases the active session — equivalent to Disconnect; lets consumers use a using block. Idempotent. Does NOT shut down the shared AACommServer process — call CloseAACommServer for that.
- field System.String DocsAppFolder = PCSuite
  the folder under "(Windows)\Documents" containing API and PCSuite settings and other data (i.e. controller About data)
- method AAComm.Services.ArrayDownloadResult DownloadArray(System.String, System.Int32, System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList<System.Double>, System.Boolean = False, System.Int32 = 60000, System.Boolean = False)
  Downloads contiguous floating-point array values and blocks for one final result. Ethernet only: on any other channel type it throws NotSupportedException. Uses Zynq stream transport when advertised by both peers; otherwise uses legacy bulk messages, or one message per element for a parameter not allowed in bulk. A timeout or disconnect is never retried because part of the array may already have been applied. Every element is checked against the controller's message table first: one whose index or value the table rules out ends the call as Rejected with that element's index and error code, and nothing is sent. A parameter the table refuses outright (unknown, read-only, not an array) throws ArgumentException.
- method AAComm.Services.ArrayDownloadResult DownloadArray(System.String, System.Int32, System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList<System.Int64>, System.Boolean = False, System.Int32 = 60000, System.Boolean = False)
  Downloads contiguous integer array values without losing 64-bit integer precision and blocks for one final result. Transport selection and retry behavior match the floating-point overload.
- method System.Void FlushDebugLog()
  Fire-and-forget asks AACommServer to write its in-memory debug log to a timestamped file NOW, without clearing the log or affecting the running session (works connected or not) there is NO acknowledgement: the newest {yyyy_MM_dd_HH-mm-ss}_Flush.log under %LocalAppData%\PCSuite\AACommServer_DebugLogs is the result no-op when AACommServer is not running
- method System.Int32 GetCanDescriptionFromParameter(System.String)
  Instance variant of GetCanDescriptionFromParameter: resolves the Complex CAN Code (CCC) for a mnemonic against this instance's parameter database. Throws on errors; requires IsConnected.
- method System.Boolean GetUserUnitsEnabled(System.Char)
  gets the per-axis User Units enabled state
- property AAComm.Services.ControllerIdentityContainer IdentityContainer { get; }
  do NOT MODIFY internal container data!! Controller Identity Container, initialized at Connect cleared at Disconnect NOT initialized by TestConnection and ConnectSilent
- property static System.Boolean IsAACommServerRunning { get; }
  API state: is AACommServer process is currently running (static property!) NOTE: execution is up to 100 msec!
- property System.Boolean IsConnected { get; }
  API state: is API connected
- property System.Boolean IsQueueEmpty { get; }
  API state: returns whether messages queue is empty. May be used whether it's safe to switch from "async" to "sync" API usage.
- property System.Boolean IsResetting { get; }
  API state: true while the transport is sleeping in the post-Reset recovery window (between OnLongOperationStarted(Reset) and OnLongOperationEnded). Useful for UI status indicators and tests that wait-for-quiet. Always false for SendReceive of a Reset (sync requests skip the recovery wait).
- property System.Int32 MaxNumOfAxes { get; }
  maximal theoretical number of axes
- field System.Int32 MaxTheoreticalNumOfAxes = 12
  maximal theoretical number of axes
- property AAComm.Services.ControllerMessagesContainer MessagesContainer { get; }
  do NOT MODIFY internal container data!! Messages Data Container, initialized fully at Connect Initialized partially (ONLY by default messages) at TestConnection and ConnectSilent cleared at Disconnect NOT initialized by TestConnection and ConnectSilent
- property System.Int32 MessagesInBulk { get; }
  returns max number of messages in a 'Bulk' packet (50) on a channel that carries a BulkMessage: Ethernet and Simulation (Returns '1' on every other channel, and while disconnected)
- property System.Int32 NumberOfAxes { get; }
  reports the maximal number of Axes supported by connected controller. (MaxTheoreticalNumOfAxes if not connected)
- event System.Action<System.String> OnCommsError
  Fatal communication error. If AACommServer was closed unexpectedly the string is AACommServerNotRunning. Suppressed only when a SendReceive was in flight AND no concurrent async Send was in flight (sync caller observes via the SR return; mixed-mode fatals still fire). Invoked synchronously on the transport receiver thread — off-load long work via Task.Run. Do NOT call API functions from the handler; no Disconnect needed after. Also raised when a SendReceive timeout closes the connection, on that caller's thread before it returns.

StartAACommServer 2. TestConnection (not mandatory, can be used to determine ControllerType) 3. Connect 4. Send and/or SendReceive (both safe from any thread, in any combination — independent FIFO pipelines for ordinary messages) 5. Disconnect 6. CloseAACommServer (not mandatory)
Signature: class AAComm.CommAPI

Members:
- event System.Action<AAComm.Shared.LongOperationType, System.Int32> OnLongOperationEnded
  Fired when a long controller operation (Reset, Save, Load, SaveUser, EventCorrect) ends. Parameters: LongOperationType identifying the operation, and the controller error code — 0 means no error (the operation succeeded); a non-zero value is the controller error code (e.g. 22 = "motor on"), or an unresolved-error sentinel when the operation ended without a parseable reply (e.g. session teardown). Fired only if the matching OnLongOperationStarted fired: a long op whose reply lands within the start-grace window raises neither edge (see OnLongOperationStarted). Do NOT call API functions while handling. Event is invoked on a background task, never before the matching OnLongOperationStarted handler has returned. Event NOT invoked if SendReceive method is used. For Reset: NOT invoked if the Reset reply was an error, if reconnecting after reset failed, or if the API was disconnected while in reset progress.
- event System.Action<AAComm.Shared.LongOperationType> OnLongOperationStarted
  Fired when a long controller operation (Reset, Save, Load, SaveUser, EventCorrect) begins. Parameter: LongOperationType identifying the operation. For Save/Load/SaveUser/EventCorrect: NOT fired when the controller replies within a short start-grace window — such a reply means the op was not long-running (e.g. an immediate ERR 22 rejecting a flash Save while the motor is on), and the reply surfaces its own result; the matching OnLongOperationEnded is suppressed too. Do NOT call API functions while handling. Event is invoked on a background task, in order with OnLongOperationEnded: a handler starts only after the handlers of every edge raised before it have returned. Event NOT invoked if SendReceive method is used.
- event System.Action<AAComm.Services.PushData.AACommPushMsgBase> OnPushMessageReceived
  Raised when an unsolicited "push" message is received from the controller. The event delivers a parsed `AACommPushMsgBase` instance (created by `AACommPushMsgBase.Parse`) and is invoked on a background `Task` to avoid blocking the receiver thread. Handlers should be aware that multiple push messages may be received in quick succession, so code re-entry and thread-safety should be considered.
- event System.Action<System.Char, System.Boolean> OnUserUnitsEnabledChanged
  Raised after the controller confirms (OK reply) a per-axis User Units enable/disable change, regardless of the path that sent it (API, Terminal, …). Fires only on an actual transition. The cache behind GetUserUnitsEnabled is updated synchronously on the receiver thread before this fires, so handlers should re-read it rather than rely on event ordering. Invoked on a background Task (like OnPushMessageReceived); consider re-entrancy and thread-safety. Args: (axis, isEnabled).
- property AAComm.Shared.ProtocolMode Protocol { get; }
  Wire protocol negotiated with AACommServer. Reflects the result after Connect: Binary against a current server, or Ascii when the client fell back to a legacy ASCII-only server (reported by ServerCompat as LegacyAscii). The consumer does not choose the protocol — this property only reports it.
- method System.Void RefreshUserUnits()
  Re-reads the full User Units configuration (per-axis enable + every group's scaling factor and units name) from the controller and refreshes the in-memory scaling cache. Blocking — uses synchronous SendReceive; call off the hot path and without parallel communications. Cheap no-op when the controller does not support User Units. Provisioning tools call this after a bulk write that bypassed the User Units config gate (AllowUserUnitsConfig), to resync the cache that the raw write left stale.
- method System.Void Send(AAComm.Services.AACommMessage)
  Asynchronous function Sends a message to the controller, over the channel connected at Connect thread-safe the event OnReplyReceived is invoked if API is in invalid state, with PcSuiteErr prefix/>
- method AAComm.Services.AACommEventArgs SendReceive(AAComm.Services.AACommMessage)
  Synchronous send/receive function Sends a message to the controller, over the CommHandler connected at Connect thread-safe — may be interleaved freely with Send for ordinary messages returns an error if called from inside a OnReplyReceived callback the reply contains the error description if the operation times out - AAComm state will be "Disconnected", and OnCommsError fires on the calling thread before this returns a sync Reset over Ethernet returns OK even when the post-reset disconnect wins the race against the reply — the disconnect is proof the reset took effect (see ResetReplyHelper)
- property AAComm.Shared.ServerCompat ServerCompat { get; }
  Classification of the AACommServer this client attached to, valid after Connect (Unknown when disconnected). Current = full feature set. The Legacy values mean the client attached in compat mode to a server started by an older application — the connection works, but features the old server lacks (correlated reply routing on LegacyAscii, channel-death events, newer version-gated features) are silently unavailable. Hosts should surface a visible warning so the user knows to upgrade the application that owns the old server.
- method System.Void SetUserUnitsEnabled(System.Char, System.Boolean)
  Sets the per-axis User Units enabled state (fire-and-forget send; does NOT validate errors). The enabled cache is not written here — it is updated ack-authoritatively when the controller confirms the change, which also raises OnUserUnitsEnabledChanged.
- property System.Boolean SkipUserUnits { get; set; }
  Consumer-wide override: when set to 'true', User Units scaling is disabled for ALL messages sent and received through this CommAPI instance. This affects every caller sharing this instance — use with caution in multi-tool environments. For per-message bypass, use SkipUserUnits instead. Always reset to 'false' at Connect. When 'true', GetUserUnitsEnabled always returns 'false' - which also drops the units from the bounds reported by GetUserUnitsData.
- method static AAComm.Shared.ConnectResult StartAACommServer(System.String = )
  Synchronous STATIC function NOT thread-safe Starts the AACommServer (if not already running) Checks to make sure process has started, up to 5 seconds should be called once, at beginning of API usage may be called again to restart the AACommServer Resolve priorities: 1. 'aaCommServerFile' function parameter: Obligatory for non-Windows clients! 2. Working directory of the executing process (Windows only!!) 3. PCSuite installation directory (if installed, Windows only!!)
- property System.Boolean SupportsArrayStreamDownload { get; }
  True when the connected controller and AACommServer both support Zynq streamed array download. DownloadArray automatically uses a legacy transport when this is false.

  Group membership array suffix, e.g. "PosUnitGrp"
- method static System.Boolean IsUserUnitsConfig(System.String)
  Returns whether the given mnemonic (without axis prefix) is a User Units config parameter: the scaling factor (FactorSuffix, e.g. "PosUnitFct") or the units-name char array (UnitsSuffix, e.g. "PosUnitUnt"). These are written only through the User Units API (ControllerMessagesContainer.TrySetUnitsSync): the units name is a multi-write char array whose adapter cache can't be kept correct by sniffing single raw writes, so raw assignments to them are rejected by the Tx-build gate. The read-only group array (GroupSuffix) and the event-driven enable parameter (UserUnitsEn) are deliberately NOT included.
- method static System.Boolean MessageAssignsUserUnitsConfig(System.String)
  Returns whether a full controller message (single axis prefix + mnemonic + optional [index] + assignment), e.g. "APosUnitFct=0.5" or "BPosUnitUnt[3]=109", assigns a User Units config parameter (see IsUserUnitsConfig). Queries (no '='/',') return false. Provisioning tools use this to decide whether a bulk write needs a post-write CommAPI.RefreshUserUnits to resync the scaling cache the raw write left stale.
- method static System.Boolean TryParseUserUnitsEnAssignment(System.String, out System.Char, out System.Boolean)
  Detects a single-axis UserUnitsEn assignment, e.g. "AUserUnitsEn=1" or "BUserUnitsEn,0". Returns false for queries (no '='/',') and for any other mnemonic. Used on the reply path to keep the enabled cache ack-authoritative and to fire the change event. Single-char axis prefix only. Spaces are removed first, matching the way the controller-message parser tokenises: "AUserUnitsEn =1" is a write the controller accepts, so the cache has to see it too.
